inline_comments.comment: Importing `configApi` and calling `getConfig()` directly inside a rendering utility function violates the project-specific rule: internal rendering functions under `rendering-util/` must not call or import `getConfig` directly — they should accept an explicit `config: MermaidConfig` parameter threaded in from callers. This import was added solely to serve the four new neo marker functions; each of those functions calls `configApi.getConfig()` independently (four `getConfig()` calls per diagram render just for markers). The fix is to remove this import, add a `config` parameter to each neo marker function, and pass `config` down from `insertMarkers` → the diagram renderer, which already holds a config reference.

The six new `-margin` marker variants added to the existing `point()`, `circle()`, and `cross()` functions (`-pointEnd-margin`, `-pointStart-margin`, `-circleEnd-margin`, `-circleStart-margin`, `-crossEnd-margin`, `-crossStart-margin`) have zero call sites anywhere in the codebase. A full-repo search confirms no file references these IDs. Because these additions live inside the shared `point`, `circle`, and `cross` functions — not the new neo-specific functions — they are silently injected into the SVG `<defs>` of *every* diagram that uses those marker types, not just ER neo diagrams. This is dead code that pollutes every affected diagram's DOM. Either wire them up to a call site or remove them.

The `crossEnd-margin` marker (line ~335) is missing `.style('stroke-dasharray', '1,0')`, while the `crossStart-margin` marker (line ~351) includes it. All other `-margin` marker pairs in this file are symmetric. This inconsistency looks like an oversight.

The PR description explicitly states: "classic and handDrawn keep `rc.line()`". However, `rc.polygon()` (via `lineToPolygon`) is used unconditionally here for *all* looks — there is no `node.look === 'neo'` guard. Every ER diagram, including classic and handDrawn, now renders divider lines as degenerate polygons with `thickness = 0.0001` instead of as lines. For the handDrawn look in particular, roughjs applies its jitter/bowing to polygons differently than to lines, so this silently changes the visual output for existing diagrams. The polygon path should only be taken when `node.look === 'neo'`; otherwise fall back to the original `rc.line()` call.

The `data-color-id` attribute assignment block is duplicated verbatim at line 70 (the early-return path for entities without attributes) and again at line 243 (the full rendering path for entities with attributes). Both blocks compute `colorIndex % borderColorArray.length` identically. Extracting this into a small inline helper or moving the assignment to a single point after the code paths converge would prevent the two copies from drifting.

`genColor` returns `''` for every theme except `'redux-color'`, but `erBox.ts` assigns a `data-color-id` attribute for *both* `'redux-color'` and `'redux-dark-color'` (via `COLOR_THEMES = new Set(['redux-color', 'redux-dark-color'])`). Because `genColor` never emits CSS rules for `redux-dark-color`, nodes in that theme get the attribute but no matching CSS — the color-cycling feature is silently broken for `redux-dark-color`. The guard should be `if (theme !== 'redux-color' && theme !== 'redux-dark-color')` (or use the same `COLOR_THEMES` set), and appropriate `bkgColorArray`/`borderColorArray` values must be confirmed for the dark variant.

The CSS attribute selector `[data-look=neo]` uses an unquoted attribute value. Per CSS spec the value should be quoted: `[data-look="neo"]`. While browsers generally accept unquoted alphanumeric values, it is non-standard and inconsistent with the quoted form used in the `genColor` CSS template above (e.g., `[data-look="${look}"]`).

`look` and `theme` are injected into the `themeVariables` spread here to make them available to `getStyles`. This conflates two distinct concerns: `themeVariables` is the designer-controlled colour/font token bag, while `look` and `theme` are top-level renderer config properties. If a future theme ever defines a token named `look` or `theme`, this would silently shadow it. A cleaner approach would be to extend the `DiagramStylesProvider` / `getStyles` signature to accept a separate config argument, or to pass a structured object rather than flattening everything into `themeVariables`.

The diagram string is built by starting with `let erCode = \`erDiagram\n\`` and then appending each line with `erCode +=` inside a `forEach`. The project rule requires multi-line diagram strings to be written as template literals with real newlines rather than via string concatenation. Consider writing a single template literal directly, or if the content must be dynamic, build an array of lines and join with `\n`.

The PR description states "Optional `colorIndex` is added to `BaseNode` for reuse by other diagrams", but `colorIndex` is only added to `EntityNode` in `erTypes.ts`. The `BaseNode` interface in `rendering-util/types.ts` is unchanged. If the intent is genuinely to support color-indexing in other diagram types, `colorIndex?: number` should be added to `BaseNode`. Otherwise the PR description should be corrected to reflect that this is ER-specific.

general_comments.comment: The PR description claims "New `requirement_arrow_neo` and `requirement_contains_neo` implement neo arrow and contains markers", but neither function exists anywhere in the codebase after these changes. A full-repo search finds no matches. Either the requirement-diagram neo markers were accidentally omitted from this PR, or the PR description is incorrect and should be updated to remove that claim.

The Cypress test file declares `const looks = ['neo'] as const` and wraps the entire suite in `looks.forEach(...)`, suggesting multi-look coverage was planned but only `neo` is tested. The `classic` and `handDrawn` looks — both of which are affected by the unconditional `lineToPolygon` change in `erBox.ts` — have no snapshot coverage here. Adding at least a `classic` entry to `looks` would catch regressions in the non-neo rendering paths.
